cases.name: Lindsey Danielle Barnett
cases.about:
Her obituary said: "Lindsey was taken from us all far too soon. She had so much left to give, so much to teach, so much love to spread. We are devastated by her tragic loss. Lindsey was born in Kansas City, Missouri April 15, 1989 and moved to Evergreen, Colorado in 1992 with her family. She attended Wilmot Elementary, Evergreen Middle School and Evergreen High School. She ran cross country and was involved in Senate and Key Club and enjoyed being in musicals and choir at the high school. Lindsey graduated from University of Northern Colorado in 2011 with a BA in Art Education K-12.

Lindsey had an incredible loving impact on her children, family, friends and students. Her kind, empathetic and generous open heart touched so many. Her radiant smile was contagious.

She had a passion for art and art history that she truly enjoyed sharing her creative nature. She started her journey of art with Evergreen Art Center in charge of programs and outreach. She taught art in schools for 15 years, including Mountain View Elementary in Parker and Stone Mountain Elementary in Highlands Ranch. Lindsey held a place in her heart for special needs children. She recently moved back to Jefferson County Schools and was teaching at Hutchinson and Westgate Elementary schools in Lakewood.

Lindsey loved painting, drawing, weaving, hiking, camping and skiing. She enjoyed traveling and history. Most of all she loved being (a) mom."
cases.narrative: On 8/13/2026 around 6:00 am, her husband called 911 frantically claiming Lindsey had “cut herself and her throat,” according to an arrest affidavit. He allegedly told police he was asleep in the basement and came up in the morning to apologize to Lindsey because the two had had a disagreement the night before. He found her bleeding in the shower, moved her head and called 911. Officers found a large amount of blood on one side of the bed, plant with dirt knocked over next to the bed and some of the soil that got dragged to the bathroom. While the bed was drenched in blood, the bathroom had little blood, police said, adding that blood patterns in the bathroom further indicated Lindsey’s body had been repositioned. Lindsey’s body also had bruises all over, including on her arms and legs, and some of them appeared to be defensive wounds, the affidavit alleges
